segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Node's `os` module — operating-system information: Node's `lib/os.js` in TypeScript over the host reads of `osinfo.c` ([ADR-01291](../adr/ADR-01291.md)). See [TDD-00024](../tdd/TDD-00024.md)/[ADR-00090](../adr/ADR-00090.md).

notes: Mirrors libuv's `uv_os_homedir` (ADR-00790): a set `$HOME` wins (an empty one included, matching Node's `""`), POSIX unset falls back to the passwd database (`getpwuid(getuid())->pw_dir`), and it throws only when that fails too; Windows reads `USERPROFILE`, falling back to the process token's profile directory (`GetUserProfileDirectoryW`, [ADR-01032](../adr/ADR-01032.md))
POSIX: Node's `getTempDir` — `TMPDIR`, then `TMP`, then `TEMP` (the first set, non-empty one), one trailing `/` stripped, else `/tmp`
On Windows: `TEMP`, then `TMP`, then `<SystemRoot|windir>\temp`, with one trailing backslash stripped unless it names a drive root — Node's exact algorithm

Real per-core `{model, speed, times: {user,nice,sys,idle,irq}}` — Linux via `/proc/cpuinfo`/`/proc/stat` parsing, Darwin via `sysctlbyname`/Mach `host_processor_info` — both verified (Darwin on Apple Silicon M4 Pro: `model` = `"Apple M4 Pro"`, live tick counters)

Darwin `speed`: `hw.cpufrequency` is unavailable on Apple Silicon (M-series removed the fixed-clock model), so a fixed `2400` MHz nominal is reported there — byte-for-byte what real Node/libuv reports on the same hardware; an Intel Mac's real value flows through unchanged ([ADR-00569](../adr/ADR-00569.md))
Darwin `times.irq` is always `0` — Mach's per-core tick array has no `irq` bucket (only user/system/idle/nice); real Node reports `irq: 0` on Darwin too, so this is parity, not a gap

Linux `speed` is cpufreq's `scaling_max_freq` (`/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuN/cpufreq/`, kHz → MHz) and `0` where cpufreq is absent — VMs and containers included — exactly what Node 22's libuv reports; `/proc/cpuinfo`'s `cpu MHz` is no longer consulted. On aarch64, with no `model name` line, `model` comes from the `CPU part` code through libuv's ARM part table (`Neoverse-N1`, `Cortex-A72`, …), else `unknown` ([ADR-00733](../adr/ADR-00733.md))
Verified on Linux and on Apple Silicon M4 Pro — `totalmem()` matches `sysctl hw.memsize`; Darwin `freemem()` (Mach `host_statistics`) returns a live free-page figure

POSIX `uname` fields; Windows `Windows_NT`, `RtlGetVersion`'s `major.minor.build` (unaffected by the manifest shim), the registry `ProductName` with libuv's `Windows 10` → `Windows 11` rewrite for build ≥ 22000, and `x86_64`/`arm64` from `GetNativeSystemInfo` — verified byte-identical to Node on Windows 11 ([ADR-01077](../adr/ADR-01077.md))
`process.arch`; the host's byte order; `devNull` is `\\.\nul` on Windows, `/dev/null` elsewhere

libuv's sources: `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` (Linux) / `kern.boottime` (Darwin) / `GetTickCount64` (Windows) seconds as a double; `getloadavg` with Windows' `[0, 0, 0]`; the affinity-set CPU count on Linux, the online count elsewhere, `GetActiveProcessorCount` on Windows ([ADR-01077](../adr/ADR-01077.md))

`{ uid, gid, username, homedir, shell }` from the effective uid's passwd entry; Windows reports `uid`/`gid` `-1`, `GetUserNameW`, `os.homedir()` and `shell: null`, as Node does ([ADR-01077](../adr/ADR-01077.md)); `{ encoding: 'buffer' }` gives Buffers and another encoding re-encodes the strings; a failed lookup throws `ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR`

An object keyed by interface name, each an array of `{ address, netmask, family, mac, internal, cidr, scopeid }` records with `scopeid` on IPv6 entries only; `getifaddrs` (up+running interfaces, MAC from the link-layer entry) / `GetAdaptersAddresses` (operational adapters, `FriendlyName`, `OnLinkPrefixLength`); `cidr` is Node's own `getCIDR` over the netmask
`getpriority`/`setpriority` (Windows: the priority class, mapped as libuv does); Node's argument validation, and `ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR` with the failed call's `info` on failure
caveats: The error's `errno`/`syscall` are copies of `info`'s, not accessors over it
Windows' priority-class mapping is compile-checked only

notes: Null-prototype `dlopen`/`errno`/`signals`/`priority` groups, `signals` frozen, the host's values in `node_constants.cc`'s order (`WSA*` codes in `errno` on Windows)
